label: Where It Happened
lede: Berlin stories told where they happened. Listen to the episodes and follow the text as I explore the places behind them.

lead.title: The Night the Gate Opened: Where It Happened, Episode 6
lead.excerpt: Episode 6 of Where It Happened: a press conference that said immediately, an officer with no new orders, and the barrier at Bornholmer Straße that went up around half past eleven on 9 November 1989.
lead.alt: Crowds and cars on the Bösebrücke at the Bornholmer Straße crossing on 10 November 1989, with a watchtower on the left

flat.title: Listening Under the Line: Where It Happened, Episode 5
flat.alt: The Glienicke Bridge at night, lit by street lamps over the water
flat.line: Episode 5 of Where It Happened: the Cold War listening tunnel under Berlin, the Glienicke Bridge where spies were swapped, and how to stand on the old border today.

flat.title: Fed From the Air: Where It Happened, Episode 4
flat.alt: C-47 transport planes lined up on the Tempelhof apron during the 1948 airlift
flat.line: Episode 4 of Where It Happened: how the 1948 Berlin airlift fed a blockaded city from the air, and where to stand at Tempelhof today.

flat.title: The Tanks at Checkpoint Charlie: Where It Happened, Episode 3
flat.alt: US Army and Soviet tanks face each other at Checkpoint Charlie in 1961
flat.line: Episode 3 of Where It Happened: the sixteen hours in October 1961 when American and Soviet tanks faced each other at Checkpoint Charlie, and where to stand today.

flat.title: The Captain of Köpenick: Where It Happened, Episode 2
flat.alt: Rathaus Köpenick with its brick tower over the summer square
flat.line: Episode 2 of Where It Happened, my weekly Berlin story podcast: a shoemaker in a secondhand captain's uniform, the Köpenick town hall, and why Germany still laughs at the story.

flat.title: The Trains That Did Not Stop: Where It Happened, Episode 1
flat.alt: The empty tiled mezzanine of Nordbahnhof S-Bahn station in Berlin
flat.line: Episode 1 of Where It Happened, my weekly Berlin story podcast: trains that ran beneath East Berlin without stopping, and four places to stand today.
